newsitem.title: INDIA: India sends in soldiers to check Tripura violence.
newsitem.headline: India sends in soldiers to check Tripura violence.

text.p: India airlifted soldiers into the northeastern state of Tripura on Tuesday to check ethnic violence after weekend clashes killed at least 35 people, officials said.
"Six aircraft with army personnel have so far arrived on Tuesday," army spokesman Arvind Thakur told Reuters in the state capital Agartala. He did not say how many soldiers were flown in.
Troops with shoot-on-sight orders combed the Khowai region where at least 35 people died on Sunday and thousands were made homeless as tribals opposed to immigrants rampaged through three villages.

Tribal separatists early on Tuesday attacked a village of Bengali settlers in Khowai region and set fire to 60 houses, police said. Agartala deputy police chief Hareram Debnath said there were no reports of casualties in Tuesday's violence.
The state government said the situation was calm but tense. "The situation in Khowai is steadily improving," it said in a statement.
Thousands of Bengali settlers are homeless and are sheltering in relief camps.
"Some 25,000 people have taken shelter in 20 relief camps," V. Tulsidas, the state's highest ranking civil servant, said on state-run television on Tuesday morning.
"Security measures in Khowai have been strengthened to frustrate the ill-designs of the militants," Tulsidas said.

Tripura's Home (Interior) Minister Samar Chowdhury ordered a police probe into allegations that security was inadequate on Sunday when tribal militants attacked a relief camp sheltering Bengali settlers.

Tripura's indigenous tribal population has been reduced to a minority by Bengali Hindu immigrants who dominate local politics and the economy. Tribal militants have been pursuing a campaign seeking a separate tribal state for 17 years.
More than 2,000 people were killed in June 1980 in the region's worst ethnic riots.

The state's communist-led government came under attack from the opposition Congress party for the surge in attacks during the past eight days by the separatist All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF). Fifty-six people have died in the attacks.
The Congress party urged President Shankar Dayal Sharma to impose direct federal rule over the state to stem violence.
